turns.text: Got it. Here's my teach-back:  I open a supplier invoice and review its line classification.  For capital-equipment lines, I choose the expense head based on the item's capital nature, not the pre-filled default — reclassifying to Plants and Machineries with the Production cost center, never small tools, per the capitalization threshold.  Then I save the corrected invoice.  Next I screen the queue for repeat billing from known suppliers.  On suspect invoices, I treat a same-amount invoice from a known repeat-biller as a suspected duplicate, not a normal bill.  I place it on hold and save, waiting for supplier confirmation before proceeding.  I also identify invoices from the UK subsidiary needing controller sign-off.  These get escalated to Pending Second Approval rather than being booked. Is that right?

Thanks. Three quick test cases, tell me if I'd get them right. Case 1: Amount (EUR) = 5,200, Expense Head = Tools and Small Equipment account. I would: block and explain — Equipment purchases above the capitalization threshold must go to the Plants and Machineries account with the Production cost center, never to small tools (85% sure). Right?
Got it. Case 2: Posting Date * = 12. I would: proceed normally, no guardrail applies (70% sure). Right?
Got it. Case 3: Company = Ltd account. I would: stop and ask — Any invoice from the UK subsidiary requires a second approval from the controller before it is booked (85% sure). Right?
Got it. That's everything. The map is published for learners.
